completion_decisions: Retain all four NREL-5MW paper cases, 2D spacing, initial sample counts, target layout-evaluation totals and native repeat counts.
Use the CC BY-NC-SA arXiv source as a manuscript and figure oracle; it contains no executable code or data.
Restrict PCE cross-validation to the largest identifiable total degree eight under the paper's 50 samples.
Replace the underdetermined full quadratic trend by identifiable additive quadratic regression and use rank-one Kriging Cholesky updates.
Correct printed Equation 21 to standard best-observed EI and declare the omitted DAKOTA variance completion.
Reconstruct the unavailable wind distribution and use declared Gaussian and ADM-Gaussian proxies without making FLORIS or CFD replay claims.
Execute 30 runs each for Cases I-III and one Case-IV run with all available Waffle cores after one/all-core H6.

machine-readable wind rose and NREL power-curve revision
PCE samples basis selected orders and cross-validation partitions
Kriging kernel trend rank handling nugget posterior variance and DAKOTA state
GA operators seeds layouts histories and per-run response arrays
ADM-RANS source mesh fields boundary conditions and all high-fidelity responses

paper.authors: Yixiao Shao and Zhenfan Wang and Shine Win Naung and Kai Zhang and Yufeng Yao and Dai Zhou
paper.title: Towards high-fidelity wind farm layout optimization using polynomial chaos expansion and Kriging model

paper_source_conflicts: Printed Equation 21 uses the current prediction instead of the historical best observation required by Equation 20 and standard EI.
Full quadratic DAKOTA trend term counts exceed the paper initial sample counts for Cases I-III.
The maximum stated PCE degree ten requires 66 bivariate total-degree terms while only 50 samples are used.
The manuscript source has no program or arrays and the final paper states that data are available on request.
The ADM-RANS assets needed for Case IV are absent, so the declared proxy cannot reproduce author CFD numbers.
Case IV labels 108.51 MW for eight 5-MW turbines, exceeding the 40-MW instantaneous farm limit; this is treated as an unnormalized direction aggregate or unit-label inconsistency.
